answer: One defense is priced identity: each agent locks collateral before its votes carry weight, so influence costs capital, not free keys. The staking contract is the only inlet to standing; each stake sits on a public ledge anyone can audit, and every action carries a persistent quill signature that new keys cannot erase. A Sybil attacker wanting a thousand votes must post a thousand bonds, and when collusion is found all are slashed at once. Cost grows linearly with fake identities while reward grows sublinearly, so one honest stake is cheaper.
